issues.summary: The full-scale confirmation of the headline de-rail (all 3375 seed600 events, complete 38-value h grid, volume_deconv default) is an explicit [RESULT PENDING] placeholder; all interior-peak evidence rests on a 494-event subsample over a seven-point grid.
issues.rationale: Disclosed placeholder (cluster jobs 5698617/5698618 queued), not a hidden omission, but a manuscript cannot go to referees with its central confirmation slot empty; the seven-point grid resolves the peak location only to +-0.03. Merges REF-M002 (math) and REF-S002 (interestingness).
issues.required_action: Fill the placeholder with the completed full-grid combined-posterior result before any submission decision; if the interior peak deviates from the expected location near 0.73, revise the de-rail claims accordingly.

issues.summary: Regime bookkeeping: the abstract designates sigma_z/z ~ 0.7 as the regime probed, but the known-truth coverage evidence lives at sigma_z/z ~ 0.1-0.2 (sigma_z = 0.035, median detected z ~ 0.3), the real-data sample is mostly near-spectroscopic, and the non-perturbative regime (sigma_z q > 1 at z_g = 0.05, per the paper's own Appendix B) is never coverage-tested by anyone, including this paper.
issues.rationale: The validation gap the paper names remains open, including for the paper's own harness; abstract and conclusions juxtapose the gap statement with the coverage tests in a way that invites the stronger closing-the-gap reading. Central to the significance framing, so not presentation polish. Merges REF-P001 (physics) and REF-S001 (interestingness).
issues.required_action: Either add a coverage run in the non-perturbative regime the abstract names (hosts at z ~ 0.05-0.1 with sigma_z ~ 0.035, catalogue-dominated), or scope abstract/introduction/conclusions to state explicitly which sigma_z/z each evidence bundle occupies and that the order-unity-ratio regime remains untested for every pipeline including this one.

issues.summary: Section 6 states 'for 3331 of the 3355 events the in-catalogue completion numerator evaluates to zero at working precision'; direct inspection of the diagnostic code shows the quoted log value is the fraction of quadrature weight outside the p_det grid (zero means full coverage), so the sentence is false as written and contradicts the same section's w_G = 0.8175 and the catalogue-only row of Table 2.
issues.rationale: Misread STAT-04 diagnostic log inherited from crux_realdata.md. The sentence's inference that the completion machinery carries most of the constraint is unsupported for the post-fix configuration, where the paper's own numbers show the opposite (catalogue-only mean 0.737 vs full 0.740). Correcting it dissolves the internal tension and strengthens 'the in-catalogue information was present all along'. Merges REF-R004 (reader) and REF-P003 (physics).
issues.required_action: Delete or rewrite the sentence to state what the diagnostic actually measured; recast channel dominance correctly (completion dominance is a pre-fix property established by the 10^3-10^5 B_num inflation; post-fix the catalogue channel dominates, w_G = 0.8175); support any retained completion-dominance claim with a per-event decomposition of the log-likelihood h-dependence into catalogue and completion channels.

issues.summary: Cross-Parkin et al. 2025 (PASA, arXiv:2502.17747) -- a published known-truth photometric-redshift dark-siren bias study using a comoving-volume prior on photo-z posteriors -- is uncited; it falsifies the introduction's implicit universal that photometric-redshift studies exist only on real data where bias cannot be tested, and strains the abstract's 'known-truth validations are almost entirely spectroscopic'.
issues.rationale: The negative gap claim survives under its full three-part conjunction (Cross-Parkin operate at sigma_z/z <~ 0.08, not the catalogue-dominated order-unity regime), and citing the work is strictly favourable (their volume-prior unbiasedness independently corroborates the repair). But because the negative universal is the paper's significance backbone, the rewrite touches abstract, introduction, codes section, and conclusions -- substantial, not cosmetic. Absorbs the significance-layer restatement REF-S003 (interestingness).
issues.required_action: Cite Cross-Parkin et al. 2025 and rewrite the validation-gap narrative as a three-way taxonomy (spectroscopic known-truth; photometric known-truth at moderate sigma_z/z, both prior-consistent and unbiased; photometric real-data), restate the surviving gap precisely as the absence of known-truth calibration at order-unity sigma_z/z in a catalogue-information-dominated analysis, and re-derive the abstract's significance sentences from the narrowed claim.

issues.summary: The field-level gap statement is argued against a literature snapshot ending mid-2023 (plus pinned-code audits); at least five 2025-2026 works in the immediate niche (gwcosmo Blinded MDC I, Borghi et al. 2026, the CHIMERA v2 code paper Tagliazucchi et al. 2025, Alfradique et al. 2025, VanWyngarden et al. 2025) are unexamined, and a referee testing the negative claim will name them.
issues.rationale: All five were verified by the literature stage as NOT filling the gap, but a negative universal at MNRAS needs the explicit adjacent-work map ('here is the complete map and the cell is empty'), and the CHIMERA v2 code paper is uncited although codes.tex pins and audits tag v2.2.
issues.required_action: Add a compact adjacent-known-truth-studies passage to Section 8 citing the Blinded MDC I, Borghi et al. 2026, Tagliazucchi et al. 2025, and Alfradique et al. 2025, stating for each why it does not occupy the catalogue-dominated sigma_z/z ~ 0.7 regime; note that Borghi et al. 2026 explicitly defer photometric redshifts, which supports the gap claim.

issues.summary: The introduction's mechanism sentence attributes sigma_z^2 suppression ('effects are second order in the redshift kernel width and therefore invisible in the spectroscopic regime') to all three defects; this is physically wrong for two of them -- the peak-density sky factor 2/(sigma_phi sigma_theta) contains no sigma_z at all, and the -17 per cent global tilt is measured with p_det point-evaluated at catalogue redshifts, already the sigma_z = 0 configuration.
issues.rationale: Mechanism misattribution propping up the hazard claim's generality: 'calibrating perfectly on spectroscopic-quality validation inputs' is demonstrated only for the kernel defect; a spectroscopic known-truth validation on an incomplete catalogue would still expose the inflated completion channel. The correct physics (validation-configuration invisibility: complete-catalogue mocks suppress the completion channel, code-vs-code comparisons are blind to common modes) is already stated in Section 8. Concurs with proof red-team missing hypothesis CLM-013-H-validation-configuration.
issues.required_action: Rewrite the introduction's mechanism sentence: attribute sigma_z^2 suppression to the kernel defect alone; attribute the invisibility of the sky-factor and global-tilt defects to the historical validation configurations, as Section 8 already does; qualify 'calibrating perfectly on spectroscopic-quality validation inputs' to the kernel defect or state the completion-suppressed-validation condition explicitly.

issues.summary: Proof red-team gate: PROOF-REDTEAM.md reports status gaps_found. Theorem-to-proof scoping repairs remain that no other ledger entry covers: (a) the 'prior-consistent' label for local_ratio satisfies only requirement (i) of the paper's own two-part definition, and the supporting lemma 'every per-galaxy constant cancels row by row' is false as phrased (CLM-006); (b) the sky-marginal bound 'valid to relative error <~1e-5' drops the source derivation's sub-percent h-smooth drift qualifier (CLM-008); (c) completeness notation is inconsistent (f(z,Omega) in framework.tex vs f(z,Omega,h) in appendix_beta_g.tex) and the h-dependence under the smooth-threshold rewriting is unpinned (CLM-020); (d) the introduction's literal universal 'every independently implemented dark-siren pipeline' is contradicted by the paper's own four-pipeline audit (CLM-013).
issues.rationale: All red-team gaps are wording/disclosure/scoping repairs -- no mathematical counterexample was found and every recomputed number reproduced exactly -- but a non-passing same-round proof red-team caps the recommendation at major_revision by policy, and each repair must land before the red-team can be re-run to status passed. The remaining red-team items (CLM-015 mass-domain clamp, CLM-019 h-neutrality corollary) are separately ledgered as REF-M004 and REF-M005.
issues.required_action: Execute PROOF-REDTEAM.md Required Follow-Up items 1-6: restore the CLM-008 error-bound qualifier or bound |rho_theta-u| over the sample; disclose the M-channel quadrature clamp; narrow the CLM-019 corollary; harmonize the completeness notation and state whether f carries h; scope the local_ratio label to numerator-denominator prior consistency and replace the row-by-row cancellation lemma with the ball-common-factors statement; replace the introduction's universal with the conclusions' scoped ex-ante form. Then re-run the proof red-team to status passed.

issues.summary: The abstract's unqualified 'the volume-deconvolved kernel is calibrated close to nominal' is supported only in the clean single-host limit; inside the full completion machinery the corrected estimator's coverage is 0.40/0.54/0.82 with a residual -0.013 bias and a compressed MAP-vs-truth slope of ~0.35, the 'decisive calibration verdict' status of the clean test is asserted rather than demonstrated, and on the real data the injected truth 0.73 coincides with the exact midpoint of the [0.60, 0.86] grid, so truth recovery and mid-grid shrinkage are not distinguished by the real-data demonstration alone.
issues.rationale: Merges REF-M007 (math), REF-P002 (physics), and REF-S006 (interestingness). The paper's prescriptive conclusion elevating coverage tests to a field prerequisite is in tension with an adopted estimator that would not pass that test at nominal inside the full machinery; scoped honestly, the same fact becomes evidence for how demanding the standard is.
issues.required_action: Scope the calibration claim to the clean single-host limit wherever it appears at abstract/conclusion level; either add a synthetic ablation showing the full-machinery residuals move with the synthetic's completeness/interloper modelling and not with the estimator, or add at least one full-machinery injection at an off-centre truth in a GLADE-like high-w_G configuration; note in Section 6 that the injected truth coincides with the grid midpoint.

issues.summary: Two of the three diagnosed defects (peak-density sky factor, global-denominator tilt) are self-inflicted implementation errors that the paper's own audit shows are structurally excluded from all four published pipelines, so the dramatic rail-flip-de-rail arc carries prophylactic rather than direct field-level significance; the genuinely field-live result (bare-kernel Eddington bias present in gwcosmo by an unenforced declaration, with coverage collapse) is the actual venue case, yet the abstract and introduction weight the drama toward the rail.
issues.rationale: Anti-conflation finding: the difficulty of the internal failure-and-repair arc must not be mistaken for field significance. The paper itself states the correct split in codes.tex; foregrounding the transferable elements (invariant, bias law, coverage methodology, audit) with the rail as exposing case study clears the MNRAS bar comfortably.
issues.required_action: Rebalance the abstract and introduction: lead the significance case with the bare-kernel bias law, coverage collapse, and validation gap; present the rail arc explicitly as the exposing case study; scope the hazard sentence to the ex-ante/future-implementations reading the conclusions already use.

issues.summary: The abstract and conclusions quote 'interior peak at the injected truth, h = 0.73' without noting the seven-point grid contains 0.73 as a grid point with +-0.03 neighbours, so peak-location agreement is demonstrated only at that resolution.
issues.rationale: The body is candid about the coarse grid and the posterior means (0.730, 0.740) add sub-grid support, but the abstract-level phrasing implies a precision the grid cannot deliver until the pending full-grid run lands.
issues.required_action: Qualify the abstract claim with the grid resolution, or update it with the full 38-point-grid result once available (resolves together with REF-R001).

issues.summary: The negative novelty claim survives only under its precise three-part conjunction (known-truth AND catalogue-information-dominated AND sigma_z/z ~ 0.7), but the abstract and conclusions restate it without the full conjunction.
issues.rationale: Negative-existence claims across a field are fragile; Section 8 draws the boundary carefully but the headline restatements drop conditions.
issues.required_action: Restate the novelty claim with its full conjunction everywhere it appears.

issues.summary: The framework section declares 'All redshifts z are CMB-frame redshifts', but the budget section discloses that the committed Section 6 baselines used heliocentric redshifts (measured net effect ~ +0.15 per cent on H0).
issues.rationale: Disclosed and quantified as negligible, but the blanket convention statement is contradicted by the data underlying the headline tables.
issues.required_action: Qualify the CMB-frame convention statement to note the Section 6 baselines predate the catalogue rebuild and used heliocentric redshifts, with the quoted +0.15 per cent effect.

issues.summary: The boundary against the nearest published counterexample-candidates (Borghi et al. 2024 known-truth photometric mocks; Cross-Parkin et al. 2025) is never quantified in the manuscript's own sigma_z/z metric, and the recovery-vs-coverage distinction is not stated where CHIMERA is discussed.
issues.rationale: Both discriminators keep the negative claim true, but neither is stated, so the claim's survival reads as assertion rather than argument.
issues.required_action: Add one or two sentences quantifying the sigma_z/z range of the Borghi et al. 2024 and Cross-Parkin et al. 2025 known-truth photometric mocks and noting the recovery-vs-coverage distinction.

issues.summary: Dated real-data anchoring: the flagship application is cited as GWTC-3 although the GWTC-4.0 cosmology paper (arXiv:2509.04348, 2025) exists, and the photometric-dark-sirens-on-real-data narrative cites only Turski et al. 2023, omitting the Palmese-line photometric measurements.
issues.rationale: LVK-community referees will immediately note the missing GWTC-4.0 reference; none of these works affects the novelty claims, but their absence weakens the paper's claim to know the field it is warning.
issues.required_action: Update the flagship-application sentence to include the GWTC-4.0 cosmology analysis and add Palmese et al. 2023 (optionally the DES Y6 x GWTC-4 measurement) alongside Turski et al. 2023.

issues.summary: The beta_G tilt percentages mix two conventions and one endpoint is misquoted: '-17.2 per cent end-to-end' is the difference of h_ref-normalized shape endpoints (multiplicative change is -15.8 per cent), and '+8.7 per cent at h = 0.60' should be +8.5 per cent per the JSON artifact.
issues.rationale: The qualitative conclusion (real, smooth, monotonic h-tilt that does not cancel) is unaffected, but the printed numbers are not reproducible without the undefined convention.
issues.required_action: Define the tilt convention once in Appendix E, correct '+8.7' to '+8.5' at h = 0.60, and relabel the raw '+93 per cent' consistently or quote the multiplicative factor only.

issues.summary: The Eddington-in-M moment quadrature domain at M <= 0 is unstated: with median sigma_rel ~ 0.98 the +/-5 sigma_M window extends far into negative mass where R_eff is undefined; the implementation clamps at max(M_g - 5 sigma_M, 1e3 Msun) but the manuscript writes Z_M unrestricted, and 'width-conservative' for the neglected skew is asserted rather than derived.
issues.rationale: The clamp is part of the definition of the moment being matched; the z-channel's analogous z >= 0 clamp received a disclosed paragraph, the M-channel's did not. Cross-references proof red-team follow-up 2.
issues.required_action: State the quadrature domain convention at M <= 0 in Appendix D, state that Z_M is taken over the physical support of R_eff, bound the truncation's effect on the first moment, and justify or soften 'width-conservative'.

issues.summary: The h^-3 neutrality lemma is exact, but the corollary 'the de-railing it produces on GLADE+ cannot be manufactured by the fix itself' outruns it: an h-neutral per-galaxy reweighting still changes the h-posterior through the data by design; the no-manufacture conclusion rests on the Section 5 calibration plus two-estimator agreement, which the 'so' in estimators.tex does not invoke.
issues.rationale: Merges REF-P008 (physics) and proof red-team follow-up 3. The lemma's real content (no spurious per-event h-tilt through the normalization) is worth keeping.
issues.required_action: Narrow the corollary to what the lemma proves and attribute the no-manufacture conclusion to the synthetic calibration and the agreement of two structurally different repairs.

issues.summary: Table C1 labels the N_g/D_g row 'exact' against the integrands of Gray eq. A10 while Section C3 declares the w_g-held-outside-the-z-integral approximation, an internal labeling tension.
issues.rationale: The rearrangement identity is airtight and the deviation honestly declared in the text, but a reader of the table alone would conclude the integrands match exactly.
issues.required_action: Change the N_g/D_g table row status to 'exact up to w_g held outside the z-integral (Section C3)' or equivalent.

issues.summary: The dt^2 self-consistent-mock-universe argument is sound, but its interpretive footprint is unstated: the catalogue-dominated character of the analysed sample (w_G = 0.8175, z <~ 0.11) exists because of the pre-correction SNR scale, and per the paper's own budget a corrected-depth campaign on GLADE+ would be completion-dominated, so the LISA-era regime designation silently assumes LSST/Euclid-depth catalogues.
issues.rationale: One sentence connecting the caveat to the regime designation resolves it; without it, the significance framing borrows realism the sample does not have.
issues.required_action: Add one sentence (Section 6 or 9) noting the catalogue-dominated character is a property of the shallow pre-dt^2 depth and that the LISA-era regime designation assumes photometric catalogues of LSST/Euclid depth.

issues.summary: The sign of the pre-fix up-rail is taken from observation, not derived: the paper derives why Defect 1 pulls h low and measures Defect 3's direction, but never explains physically why the inflated peak-density completion channel prefers the upper grid edge, so the sign-flip prediction is half-derived.
issues.rationale: The chain's logic survives (opposite-sign superposition implies flip under staged repair), but 'the predicted fingerprint of two opposing mis-normalizations' reads as if both signs were understood mechanistically.
issues.required_action: Add a brief physical explanation of the up-rail direction, or state explicitly that it is an empirical element of the chain while the down-pull sign is the derived one.

issues.summary: The Gaussian photometric-redshift likelihood is a strong assumption in exactly the order-unity sigma_z/z regime the paper designates: real photo-z error distributions there are skewed with catastrophic outliers, never discussed although Rubin-LSST and Euclid are named in the significance claims.
issues.rationale: The prior-consistency invariant is kernel-agnostic, but every quantitative calibration statement is Gaussian-specific; the nearest known-truth photometric study (Cross-Parkin et al. 2025) explicitly includes outlier models.
issues.required_action: Add one scope sentence: the quantitative bias law and coverage results assume Gaussian per-galaxy redshift likelihoods; the prior-consistency invariant does not; skewed/outlier-bearing photo-z likelihoods are outside the present calibration.

issues.summary: Venue-fit conditionality: the 'LISA-era' motivation is carried by a mock population that is not a LISA-era population (physical-SNR >= 200, z <~ 0.11, product of the pre-dt^2 scale defect); MNRAS realism expectations are met only if the sample is consistently presented as a controlled estimator testbed.
issues.rationale: The estimator-comparison logic survives; the residual risk is presentational and removable with one or two sentences wherever LISA-era framing appears.
issues.required_action: Audit every 'LISA-era' occurrence to ensure it reads as motivation for the methodology rather than as a description of the analysed sample, and add the REF-P005 sentence.

issues.summary: Submission placeholders remain: author 'TBD', affiliation 'TBD', and acknowledgements 'TBD --- funding, compute ... collaborators'.
issues.rationale: Purely administrative; the manuscript cannot be submitted with these in place.
issues.required_action: Fill author list, affiliations, and acknowledgements before submission.

issues.summary: Minor grid inconsistency: the de-rail matrix uses h in [0.60, 0.86] (rail at 0.86) while the postmortem's full-sample bare run uses a 0.01-spaced grid on [0.60, 0.87] (rail at 0.87); the abstract quotes only the former.
issues.rationale: Both rails are edge results and the paper warns that unconstrained maxima may lie outside the grid; harmonizing removes a small reader stumble.
issues.required_action: Add a one-line note reconciling the two grids.

issues.summary: The EMRI statistical-siren lineage omits MacLeod & Hogan 2008 (the original EMRI statistical-redshift H0 proposal) and Del Pozzo, Sesana & Klein 2018, the direct ancestors Laghi et al. 2021 build on.
issues.rationale: Minor genealogy gap that LISA-cosmology referees will expect closed.
issues.required_action: Cite MacLeod & Hogan 2008 and Del Pozzo, Sesana & Klein 2018 in the EMRI dark-siren lineage sentence.

issues.summary: Bibliography hygiene: 9 uncited orphan entries seeded from Paper B remain in references.bib, and the Babak:2023lro texkey/year inconsistency (arXiv:2108.01167 is 2021, INSPIRE texkey Babak:2021mhe) is unresolved.
issues.rationale: Tracked in paper_a/BIBLIOGRAPHY-AUDIT.json; cited-entry metadata spot-verified as correct. Mechanical cleanup.
issues.required_action: Prune the 9 orphan entries and either rekey Babak:2023lro to Babak:2021mhe or record the deliberate key choice.
